extracted.intended_audience: program evaluators, MER organizers, mathematics faculty involved in mathematics-education reform
extracted.subtask_description: Survey instruments and evaluative criteria for assessing the MER Forum workshops and network effectiveness, including measures of individual and departmental outcomes, workshop design, participant demographics, and department climate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform (Jenness & Barley definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge MER's effectiveness by the extent to which MER encourages the development of new working relationships both within the mathematics community and among other related disciplines, and whether broad changes have occurred within the mathematics community in addition to local or individual types of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Jenness’ & Barley’s definition of systemic reform (see chapter 4). Distinguish local/individual changes from broad/systemic change; look for evidence of new cross-disciplinary relationships and community-level change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual-level outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Three most common types of individual changes: (1) enhanced awareness of educational issues, (2) strengthened feelings of support, and (3) improved classroom pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect specific examples of each type; consider rate and depth of change when inferring contribution to systemic reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental/network-level systemic change
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which departmental workshops (group attendance from a department, involvement of department chairs, listserver participation, inter-departmental collaboration) produce quicker and more likely systemic reforms than individual-level involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for presence of key decision-makers (department chairs), critical mass of participants, follow-up activities (planning grants, interdisciplinary initiatives), and the ability to influence central administration or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop design effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of workshops as determined by structure: an overarching theme plus breakout sessions to accommodate specific interests; built-in informal contact time (e.g., meals) to foster personal comfort and spontaneous exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether workshop structure maximized positive outcomes (participants' perception of gaining insights, formation of collaborations, initiating new projects). Evidence includes spontaneous initiatives and exchange programs discussed/formed at the workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of face-to-face contact / 'hallway conversations'
rubrics_metrics.description: Which beneficial aspects of the workshop could only be obtained by being physically present (nuances: eye contact, closeness, unplanned encounters) versus what could have been achieved via written materials, telephone, or video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask participants to list aspects uniquely benefited by physical presence and those that could be delivered by other media; evaluate tradeoffs of resource use for face-to-face events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between prescriptive and laissez-faire approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: MER's role as a support mechanism should avoid being overly prescriptive (which might alienate mathematicians) and avoid being too laissez-faire (which may accomplish little); success judged on striking an appropriate balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect participant perceptions of MER's guidance level and whether it facilitated participation without alienation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of MER activities (postsecondary vs K-12 coordination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that most participants and MER focus efforts at the postsecondary level despite stated K–12 emphasis; criterion includes need for improved coordination with mathematics educators and K–12 organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure extent of K–12 engagement and coordination; evaluate whether MER activities align with funding proposals' stated emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographics: gender/race/ethnicity/birth year
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect participant demographic information: gender, racial/ethnic classification, and year of birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard demographic items (multiple-choice categories provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: How participants found out about MER
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric asking respondents how they found out about MER (mailing from MER; recommended/informed by colleagues; MER newsletters; posted announcements; other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess outreach channels and recruitment effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at MER banquet and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether participant has attended a MER banquet at the Joint Mathematics Meetings and whether they would recommend it to colleagues (yes/no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple yes/no items to gauge perceived value of banquet events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness of MER newsletter and useful sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the MER Forum newsletter helpful? Which sections are helpful (information on basic MER activities; feature articles on programs/projects; essays on state/future of mathematics education; information on MSEB; other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary helpfulness item plus check-all sections to identify valued content types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and reading of CBMS Issues volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Are respondents aware of MER publications in the CBMS Issues in Mathematics Education volumes? Have they read any?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes/no items to measure penetration and readership of MER publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at MER special sessions at Joint Mathematics Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether respondent has attended MER special sessions at the Joint Mathematics Meetings (yes/no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used with follow-up items about influence and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of MER special sessions on attendance decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent did the existence of MER special sessions at the Joint Mathematics Meetings influence your decision to attend the Meetings and to attend a MER workshop? Response scale: 1 not at all, 2 a little, 3 considerably, 4 extremely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likert-style scale; collect explanations if respondents indicate considerable/extreme influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of special sessions and CBMS volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent were the special sessions useful to you? To what extent are the CBMS Issues volumes useful? (1–4 scale). If useful, please explain how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likert items with optional open-ended elaboration to capture nature of usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at MER workshops (which workshops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether respondent has attended a MER workshop; if yes, which of the listed workshops (multiple selection from specific dates/locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures experience timeline and which events influenced participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for attending MER workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist of reasons for attending (colleague recommendation; department chair recommendation; invited speaker; invited to make small group presentation; meet people who share interests in math education reform; meet people who share mathematical research interests; trip paid by others; visit city/university; meet MER co-directors; exchange ideas with peers; interested in workshop theme; other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple-response item to understand motivations for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest educational degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's highest degree (Bachelor’s, Master’s, Ph.D. in Math, Ph.D. in Math Education, Ph.D. other, Ed.D., other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard education-level metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership in professional organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Which professional organizations does the respondent belong to? (AMS, MAA, SIAM, AWM, NCTM, AMATYC, AERA, other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to profile networks and disciplinary alignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty experience (years at current and other schools)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many years have you been a faculty member at your present school? How many years at other schools?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric items to capture career stage and mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of reform issues due to MER
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement item: 'I am more aware of the issues in math education reform as a result of the MER Forum.' (1 strongly disagree – 4 strongly agree). If 3 or 4, provide up to two specific examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likert plus open-ended examples to document concrete awareness gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of MER duplicating other services / unique aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement item: 'MER duplicates services provided by other organizations.' Plus request to indicate unique aspects of MER or aspects duplicated by others (1–4 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects comparative judgments of MER's niche or redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-workshop comfort contacting colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement item: 'After participating in one MER workshop, I felt comfortable calling/contacting MER colleagues I had just met about professional matters.' (1–4 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures networking confidence and perceived collegiality formed at events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in own teaching attributed to MER
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement item: 'I have changed my own teaching because I have been involved with MER.' Follow-ups: attribute impetus to MER newsletters/networking; attribute impetus to MER workshops. Provide two examples of changes in classroom teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary/Likert with attribution probes and concrete examples to validate claimed practice change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of contacting MER colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Since your first MER workshop, how frequently have you contacted MER colleagues about: a) personal teaching issues, b) mathematics education reform issues, c) mathematical research issues? Response categories: never, once, 2–5 times, 6–10 times, more than 10 times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies ongoing networking and collaboration intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to attend another MER workshop under cost conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Would you attend another MER Forum workshop if (a) all expenses were paid? (b) you had to pay for your own transportation and conference fee? (c) you had to pay all your own expenses including room and board? (yes/no for each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses sensitivity to cost and financial barriers to participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority reforms needed in mathematics education (open response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please describe the two most vital reforms needed in mathematics education in your opinion (e.g., types of curriculum, pedagogy, or assessment improvements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended responses used to aggregate perceived reform priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most positive feature of the MER Forum (open response)
rubrics_metrics.description: In your opinion, what is the most positive feature of the MER Forum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended; solicits single top-perceived strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion for improving MER (open response)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you could make one suggestion regarding how to improve MER, what would it be?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended improvement prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness of MER in furthering respondents' projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Has your association with the MER Forum been helpful to you in terms of furthering the goals of your own projects? (yes/no). If yes, please elaborate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits evidence of concrete project support or networking benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present academic rank
rubrics_metrics.description: If you work in an academic institution, what is your present rank? (Graduate student, Instructor, Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor, Other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures career stage distribution among participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting a workshop and perceived benefits/drawbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you hosted a workshop at your institution? (yes/no). What do you perceive as benefits and drawbacks to hosting a workshop (and difficulty/ease of working with MER)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents institutional capacity and perceived burden/benefit of hosting events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of involvement in specific reform activities (past two years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a 1–4 scale (not at all, a little, considerably, very), indicate extent of involvement with activities: a) K–12 curriculum reform, b) Undergraduate curriculum reform, c) Increasing participation of underrepresented minorities, d) Increasing participation of women, e) Undergraduate programs for math majors, f) Reform related to graduate mathematics education, g) Undergraduate remedial courses, h) Calculus reform, i) Undergraduate programs for pre-service teachers, j) Programs for in-service teachers, k) Involvement with specific groups of K–12 students (e.g., gifted & talented or special needs), l) Reform efforts at the school district level, m) Reform efforts from statewide initiatives, n) Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized scale allows comparison across reform activity types; respondents may circle one number per item and provide details where asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of primary reform involvement (open response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the type of mathematics education reform with which you are most involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-ended summary to contextualize quantitative involvement responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate of departmental faculty involvement in activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate number of faculty in your department involved in: K–12 math education reform, Undergraduate math education reform (for both math and non-math majors), Undergraduate teacher preparation reform, Graduate math education reform for math grad students, Graduate math education reform for math ed grad students, Teacher enhancement for in-service teachers, Research mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects departmental capacity and distribution of effort across activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of faculty in department
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the total number of faculty in your department?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute proportions from faculty involvement estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of formal/informal collaboration with education departments
rubrics_metrics.description: How often do you formally or informally collaborate with educators in education departments on your campus? Response options: never, once per year, once or twice per semester, once or twice per month, more than twice per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures cross-departmental collaboration frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time allocation among professional activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Using provided definitions, divide your work time among: Teaching; Mathematics Research/Scholarship; Mathematics Education Reform Activities; Service; Administration; Other. Provide # of hours/week you spend on each, and # of hours your department prefers for promotion/tenure/merit raise decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric hours and departmental preference capture workload balance and institutional reward structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental climate: value and acceptance of reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-point Likert items: a) 'Involvement in mathematics education reform is highly valued in my department.' b) 'In my department, the atmosphere toward mathematics education reform is one of acceptance and support.' (1 strongly disagree – 4 strongly agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess department-level attitudes toward reform work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental climate: change in attitude and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Item: 'During the past five years, the atmosphere in my department toward mathematics education reform has changed, becoming more positive towards it.' (1–4 scale). If 3 or 4, provide two specific examples of recent departmental attitude changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines quantitative trend perception with qualitative examples to document attitudinal shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department support for new projects and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Item: 'During the past five years, new projects and programs related to mathematics education have been supported by my department.' (1–4). If 3 or 4, provide two specific examples of new educational projects or programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses concrete departmental support and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of literature and mathematics educators
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement items: a) 'I usually consult literature in the field of educational research for information about mathematics education reform.' b) 'I usually consult mathematics educators (professionals in education) for research about mathematics education reform.' (1–4 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures reliance on educational research and professional collaborators in reform work.
